newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan law won't affect on banks' futures trades.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan law won't affect on banks' futures trades.

text.p: The proposed futures trading law under consideration by Taiwan's parliament will not regulate the money market financial derivatives of banks and other financial institutions, officials said on Tuesday.

Interest rate and foreign currency futures will remain under the control of the central bank despite language in the draft futures law that gives the finance ministry oversight of derivatives, a central bank official said by telephone.
Nothing would change for money market derivatives traded at banks, the official said.
"The Ministry of Finance is trying to establish Taiwan's futures trading law, but those financial derivatives that now are traded at banks will remain under our control," he said.
Finance ministry officials said the proposed futures law aimed to secure the establishment of Taiwan's futures exchange.
"The futures law is for establishment of a futures exchange, not for trying to manage the central bank's money market operations," Vice Minister of Finance Wu Chia-sheng told Reuters by telephone.

Wu said the draft law also would not regulate financial futures trading by banks and bills companies, including bond interests, gold margin leverage trade and equity swaps. The central bank began allowing equity swaps on August 28.
The finance ministry and Securities and Exchange Commission have said they hope the exchange can open by July.
